title: Does anyone even like this f*ck ass combat? lol
author: Kind-Introduction-15
selftext: I am exploring combat ideas, one of the ones I had was a completely mouse driven physics based procedural combat in first person. I am wondering if anyone at all likes this. I think its pretty funny/fun, but I am not sure how it would work outside of this little test zone. I want magic and other weapons too but I am not sure. Its still early, but I am mainly looking for feedback to either make this better or if its even worth working on.

comments.body: KCD is a little less mouse driven but this kinda reminded me of that! Looks like it could be fun but I'd have to actually try it to see if maybe it'd just get tiring. I could imagine people getting wrist pain from it lol

replies.author: kilographix
replies.body: What type of environment is it running in? Is it real time multiplayer or a single player game? You could do a more gesture based combat that takes a mouse gesture like you are doing but pauses or slows time when you trigger it to allow for better precision.

comments.author: brother_spirit
comments.body: Have you played Mordhau or Chivalry? Worth giving those a go as that is fundamentally what you're going for here. They have pretty goated first person / third person weapon combat with ragdolls, etc. Mordhau IMO is the best of the best. Give it a download - you can and will get curb stomped by the handful of grinders left on the server. Recommended.

replies.body: Yes! I actually really love those games, another good one but its single player is Dark Messiah, initially I was doing something like that but animations are hard to come by on a budget

replies.author: brother_spirit
replies.body: HOMM rules! Probably best staying with procedural until you have a combat system you like. Chamber/morph/timed parry/riposte/feint planned? Depends how fancy you want to go with it but from there a nicely rigged 3D asset will be worth it's weight in gold to you.

comments.author: H0wlingDingo
comments.body:
I used to work at a medium to large indie large open world grand RPG game company and a system like this was one of my tasks this was before they switched to another engine from unreal engine 

But I did finish the system and play tested it for a bit so I am uniquely qualified to talk about this so here are my recommendations honestly kinda wish I had AI when I first did this this type of system can be a pain specially if you plan to see your characters hands or body.

Ok first things first when swinging in real life if you swing most of the time you can’t stop that swing you are committing to that swing so in your system as the blade get closer to middle it should speed up that is unless you never passed that speed threshold 

On small swings like how you were doing little fast swing up and down it isn’t really how you use a sword I fixed this issue my self by slowing down the sword that is unless you have the correct power/speed threshold for a swing think of it as a slower point in space following your mouse and your doing some form of lerp between the two point

I see you blade is all ready tipping a bit which is good depending on if you want it to feel less float or not this is up to what you think feels best you can have 7 blade starting points that is from above from top left from left from bottom left from top right from right from bottom right.   There is no from bottom as that is not really a sword position but these locked points are what you blade switches between if you don’t pass that speed threshold it will look like KCD stance switch you know that star in the middle of your screen in combat in KCD and when switching you could do animations to make it smoother but I am going to expect not so you can just do a type of lerp between the switch points 

As above do the same system for blocking free blocking can feel difficult some times if you want that’s fine but adjust the locked stance system to fit block in my opinion feels better

The sword swinging is the easiest part of a system like this if you plan to add a player character I am unsure if AI can make it look good yet you might need a game engine for that.

And I do recommend locking blade movement behind a speed threshold as you may have noticed that looking while swinging the blade is problematic this is another way to make that issue a little better 

But the systems good so far can’t show any of my work to help you so sorry about that but hope this helps you make your system better

replies.author: H0wlingDingo
replies.body: Forgot to mention go play some half sword it is the peak of this type of system

replies.author: Kind-Introduction-15
replies.body: thank you very much for the feed back, I am working on godot, but AI cant seem to understand hands and wrist for models. I am going to try applying a lot of what you said to my game for experimenting, and I plan on making another post about it

replies.author: H0wlingDingo
replies.body:
i am not too sure how godot works its not the engine I use but it should be possible. if adding character models is something you were going to do and if so i will explain a little on the concept of making a Rig 

lets say your going to use a full body character your going to want to get the location of the sword this will allow you to point the body in the direction of the sword so lets say you move the sword to the left of you the upper spine bones will turn before the lower ones so that means less of a look at strength as you get closer to the pelvis/hips you can have a slight tilt side to side but in most cases the spine will be straight.  
  
arms and hands your going to need to attach them to the weapon most cases developers will attach the sword to the hand this is because in most cases the procedural animation is slower meaning you might see slight lag between the hand and weapon so locking the weapon to the hand will stop this this does mean that you might have to rework your system tho : (    but the arms and hands should be rather easy to get working you don't need a complicated IK set up however you might have some trouble when swapping swing directions as the characters wrists will need to be fliped a good way to understand this is grap your tv remote of a thing shaped like it and start swinging it in front of you with one hand and two hands as you slowly swing back and forth you will understand how the characters arms and wrists should look.

I have places a godot video on IK bellow but you can try to use AI to get this working but you may need to learn some stuff about IK but I hope this will help you make your game and understand where the pit falls are.

  
here are some resources that may help you 

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MbaPDWfbNLo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MbaPDWfbNLo) \- For godot this isn't as detailed as the unreal one but it will help you get started in godot

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hhcpSXJ2zak](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hhcpSXJ2zak) \- This one is for unreal engine but it may help you understand the process

comments.author: Accomplished_Rock695
comments.body: There are lots of actual collision games. The hardest part is selling the grounded nature of the animation. Most gamers are used to the floaty sword swings everywhere style. Going physics based is anything but that. There needs to be recoil. It has to ride up the arms. Otherwise you are in the gap.
